newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-STRAWBERRY HAS SURGERY, OUT 4-6 WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-STRAWBERRY HAS SURGERY, OUT 4-6 WEEKS.

text.p: New York Yankees slugger Darryl Strawberry, who has been on the disabled list for more than two months, underwent surgery to remove a defect in his left thigh bone Wednesday, the team said.
Doctors believed Strawberry would be sidelined four to six weeks, the Yankees said in a statement.
The surgery was performed by Dr Russell Warren at the Hospital for Special Surgery in New York.
Strawberry, 35, played with a noticeable limp while going 4-for-15 with two homers and six RBI during a four-game rehabilitation stint with Triple-A Columbus earlier in the month.

He has been on the disabled list since April 11 due to fluid on his left knee after going hitless in 14 at-bats with the Yankees. Strawberry batted .262 with 11 homers and 36 RBI in 63 games last season.
An earlier rehab assignment with Double-A Norwich also had to be cut short after one game when he was diagnosed with irritated cartilage under his left kneecap.
